watch_outs: Hurricane Straps & Wind Mitigation: Florida requires specific wind-resistant construction methods that can significantly impact insurance rates Reddit users emphasize getting a wind mitigation inspection—hurricane straps, secondary water barriers, impact windows, and roof-to-wall connections can reduce insurance by 20-45%. Any roofing work should include these upgrades.

Impact Windows & Hurricane Shutters: Florida Building Code requires impact-rated glazing or protection in most of the state Large-missile impact zones (most of South Florida) require impact glass or approved shutters. Reddit users report that impact windows pay for themselves in insurance savings within 5-10 years. Verify products are Florida Product Approved.
Flood Zone & Elevation Requirements: Much of Florida is in flood zones with strict requirements for renovations The "50% rule" means if improvements exceed 50% of the structure

Moisture & Mold Prevention: Florida Any work that exposes wall cavities risks mold if not properly dried before closing up. Reddit users insist on dehumidification during construction, proper vapor barriers, and mold-resistant materials in wet areas.

Florida Contractor Licensing: Florida has strict contractor licensing—verify at myfloridalicense.com Florida requires state licenses for contractors, and local jurisdictions often require registration too. Reddit warns about "storm chasers" with out-of-state licenses. Always verify at myfloridalicense.com and check for complaints.
